# Appeal of Denial — Shoulder Labral / Instability Repair (CPT 29806)

**Riley Hayes**
Member ID: W890739050
[Street address]
[City, State ZIP]
[Phone]

**Date:** [Date of this letter]

**To:** Sunflower Health Plan — Appeals and Grievances
[Appeal address printed on my denial letter]

**RE: Appeal of adverse benefit determination dated 2026-08-18**
**Reference number:** POC-5BC96481D7-41351
**Member:** Riley Hayes — Member ID W890739050
**Plan:** Sunflower Health Plan (Commercial/ACA), Kansas
**Service denied:** Shoulder labral / instability repair, CPT 29806
**Governing policy:** 2026 Evolent MSK Surgery Guidelines, effective 2026-07-01 — https://www1.radmd.com/sites/default/files/2026-05/2026%20Evolent%20Musculoskeletal%20Surgery%20Guidelines.pdf

---

Dear Appeals Reviewer,

I am appealing the denial of prior authorization for the shoulder labral/instability repair (CPT 29806) requested by my surgeon, Dr. Duval, MD. The notice dated 2026-08-18 states that the imaging findings submitted do not support the medical necessity of the requested procedure. I am asking the plan to reconsider that decision, because the imaging in my chart is exactly the imaging finding the plan's own published criteria call for, and my records also document the history and exam findings those criteria describe.

I am quoting below only from the 2026 Evolent MSK Surgery Guidelines, the document listed above. Each quoted line is followed by the matching information from my medical records.

## The plan's criteria, and what my records show

The guidelines introduce the relevant pathway this way:

> "Bankart repair of an acute labral tear may be necessary when all the following criteria are met:"

That sentence ends in a colon and introduces a list of conditions that I have not been given in full. I am addressing the criteria I do have in front of me, and I ask the plan to identify in writing every criterion it actually applied to my request.

**Imaging — the stated basis for the denial.** The guidelines state:

> "Labral tear/Bankart lesion on MRI or CT imaging"

and

> "MRI evidence of a labral tear with or without bony Bankart fracture of the glenoid. Cases with a history of frank anterior dislocations without MRI evidence of a labrum tear will be reviewed on a case-by-case basis."

My MR arthrogram of the shoulder dated 2026-06-20 reports an anteroinferior labral tear (Bankart lesion) with a small Hill-Sachs lesion, glenoid bone loss under 10 percent, and an intact rotator cuff. That is a labral tear/Bankart lesion identified on MR imaging. The second criterion above reserves case-by-case review for dislocations *without* MRI evidence of a labral tear; my study affirmatively shows the tear, so that caveat does not apply to me. I would appreciate knowing, specifically, what the reviewer found lacking in this study.

**History of instability.** The guidelines state:

> "History of an acute event of instability (subluxation or dislocation) or acute onset of pain following activity"

and

> "Recurrent instability (two or more episodes of subluxation or dislocation)"

My records document three anterior dislocations since my symptoms began, the most recent of which was reduced in the emergency department.

**Symptoms.** The guidelines state:

> "Symptoms of pain, catching/popping, or instability"

My records document 14 months of recurrent episodes of shoulder instability with apprehension. I avoid overhead reaching and I cannot return to my job, which requires lifting.

**Physical examination.** The guidelines state:

> "Clinical exam findings demonstrate positive apprehension test, positive relocation test, positive labral grind test, or objective laxity with pain"

and

> "Physical examination findings demonstrate positive apprehension test, positive relocation test, positive labral grind test, or objective laxity with pain (PE is not required if there has been a recent episode of instability or there is a radiographic evidence of any prior dislocation)"

My examination documents a positive apprehension test and a positive relocation test, with increased anterior translation on load-and-shift and full strength. The guidelines also state:

> "Exam findings demonstrate positive load-and-shift test, jerk test, glenohumeral grind test, or objective laxity with pain or profound weakness"

The increased anterior translation on load-and-shift in my exam note speaks directly to that line.

**Range of motion.** The guidelines state:

> "Range of motion is not limited by stiffness upon physical exam (PE is not required if there has been a recent episode of instability)"

Please refer to my surgeon's examination note for the recorded range-of-motion findings [range-of-motion findings from Dr. Duval's examination note, if requested]. I would also note the parenthetical in the plan's own language: examination is not required where there has been a recent episode of instability, and my records document a dislocation reduced in the emergency department [date of the emergency department visit].

**Non-operative treatment.** The guidelines state:

> "Failure of at least 12 weeks of non-operative treatment (unless presenting as a traumatic tear in a competitive athlete at any level) that includes any TWO of the following:"

This line also ends in a colon, and I have not been given the list that follows it. What my records show is 16 weeks of supervised physical therapy from 2026-03-16 to 2026-07-06, 18 visits completed, focused on rotator cuff and scapular stabilizer strengthening, with activity modification, documented in the physical therapy discharge note; and NSAIDs taken for 4 months during flares. No injection was given, as it was not indicated for instability. Sixteen weeks of documented supervised therapy exceeds the 12-week period the plan itself sets out. If the plan believes a specific item from the unreproduced list is missing, I ask that it say which one.

**Criteria that describe a different presentation.** The guidelines also contain lines addressing posterior labral tears and hyperlaxity without traumatic dislocation, including "MRI findings of posterior labral tear"; "Individual has recurrent instability due to hyperlaxity or mobility and no traumatic dislocation"; "Physical exam supports repeatable increased glenohumeral joint translation (greater than 1 cm of movement during the sulcus test)"; and "MRI with arthrogram confirms capsular laxity and excludes Bankart and Kim lesions (tear between posterior labrum and articular cartilage), or glenoid erosion." These describe presentations different from mine. My documented condition is an anteroinferior (Bankart) labral tear with three anterior dislocations. Separately, the guidelines state:

> "No radiographic evidence of degenerative disease (e.g., posterior glenoid cartilage loss, subchondral glenoid cysts, mucoid degeneration of labrum, narrowing of joint space with posterior humeral head subluxation on axillary x-ray or axial MRI images)"

My 2026-06-20 MR arthrogram report, as summarized in my packet, describes the labral tear, a small Hill-Sachs lesion, glenoid bone loss under 10 percent, and an intact rotator cuff; no degenerative findings of that kind are reported.

Also documented in my file: no active infection, no untreated substance use, BMI 29, non-smoker.

## Request for the criteria the plan applied

I am asking the plan, in writing, for the specific medical policy and clinical review criteria used to deny this request — including the full text of any criteria list that the excerpts above introduce but do not reproduce, and the reviewer's explanation of which criterion my imaging failed to satisfy. The plan holds those criteria; I do not. I understand the plan uses Evolent for musculoskeletal surgery review, and that Evolent publishes these guidelines publicly at the link above. Please confirm whether the 2026 Evolent MSK Surgery Guidelines were the criteria applied to my request, and if a different document or internal standard was used, please provide it.

## What I am asking for

I ask that Sunflower Health Plan overturn the 2026-08-18 denial and authorize CPT 29806 as requested by Dr. Duval, who has documented that this procedure is needed. My surgeon's office and I are glad to supply any additional records, and I request a peer-to-peer discussion with my surgeon if that would help the reviewer.

**Deadline and where this is being sent.** Per the notice dated 2026-08-18, my appeal must be received within 180 days of that date, by **2027-02-14**. I am submitting this appeal to the appeal address printed on my denial letter. I understand I may also file online at ambetterhealth.com by selecting Kansas and using that state's appeal/grievance form, or by calling the number on my member ID card, and that the address on my denial letter is the one to use for mail.

Please send your written determination to me at the address above, along with the criteria requested. Thank you for taking another look at this.

Sincerely,

_______________________________
**Riley Hayes**
Member ID: W890739050
Reference number: POC-5BC96481D7-41351

Date: [Date]
